You use tag questions to ask for clarification and confirmation.
Sometimes they are used in an affirmative sentence but with a negative adverb.
Question tags are short questions at the end of statements.
They are mainly used in speech when we want to:

• confirm that something is true or not, or
  • to encourage a reply from the person we are speaking to.

A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag.
Use this when you think the other person will agree by saying ‘yes'

The adverbs never, rarely, seldom, hardly, barely and scarcely have a negative sense. Even though they may be in a positive statement, the feeling of the statement is negative. We treat statements with these words like negative statements, so the question tag is normally positive.

To deliver a great presentation there are some skills that you need. Below are some skills that will help you give a great presentation.

• Begin with the end in mind.
    • Figure out what you want your presentation to do for you: persuade, inform or inspire?
    • Develop a presentation with the necessary components.

• Keep it simple.
    • Don't try to put too much information in the presentation.
    • Keep PowerPoint slides simple. (3 bullet points per slide)

• Don't wing it, but don't memorize.
    • Only memorize the important parts.
    • Use cue cards if you need to make notes.
    • Practice your presentation out loud.

• Include lots of questions.
    • Use questions in your presentation to engage and persuade others.

• Focus on quality, not quantity.
    • Pick one piece of information that you think would be beneficial and focus your presentation around that.

• Smile!
    • During the presentation, smile, take deep breaths and pause.

Sophie: Kelly, what's the best way to prepare a presentation?
Kelly: Well, first you need to think about the purpose. Do you want to inform, persuade, inspire? Don't start writing until you know your purpose.
Sophie: Okay. Then what?
Kelly: Remember to keep it simple. Don't try to include too much information. It should be easy to follow.
Sophie: Should I use Powerpoint?
Kelly: You can but only have 3 bullets per slide. And always include some questions in your presentation. They engage your listeners and encourage exploring possibilities.
